title: The legacy criteria of RWB-E4-044 are generic, carry no proceeds data and the split plan gives the slice no requirement id
source: Legacy RWB-E4-044 (Story, Acceptance criteria, Data, Test cases); FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 A2.4.4.1 (AC-P8-004-01) and A2.4.4.3; work package line for RWB-P8-E4044-APP (reqs empty)
description: The story owns two legacy criteria word for word and both are generic. AC1 reads 'Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place / When its trigger arrives / Then matches money from an auction, a broker or the LED to the right case / Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version' and AC2 reads 'Given the decision log cannot be written / When the action is taken / Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003'. The four legacy test cases repeat those rows with no proceeds-specific value: no case, no receipt, no source, no amount and no business date. The FSD keeps FEAT-PAY-04 and its main success criterion AC-P8-004-01 is one line marked 'Written one epic ahead', so the module adds no value either. The split plan carries no requirement id for this slice, which is why section 18 traces the criteria to FEAT-PAY-04 and AC-P8-004-01 rather than to a requirement row. The story keeps both criteria unchanged and states its own synthetic proceeds set, which is where the case, receipt, source and amount of the test cases come from.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-044 AC1 and AC2 as quoted; legacy test cases TC-E4-044-01 'Match auction and enforcement proceeds' and TC-E4-044-02 'Not recorded' with no data column; FSD P8 v3 A2.4.4.1 AC-P8-004-01 'The data and rules it needs are in place / The trigger arrives / The result is recorded with its rule version / Written one epic ahead'; the FSD 'Requirements served' table of P8 is empty.
owner_role: P8 business analyst and the FSD owner
proposed: Have the Payment module owner confirm the proceeds data set the E4 build tests on (case, account, receipt of source AUCTION or LED on the business date, amount, matched_to SALE_PROCEEDS and the unmatched case) and carry it into the Story test cases tab of the Test Cases master under the same four test case IDs; add the requirement row of FEAT-PAY-04 to the 'Requirements served' table of FSD P8 in its next version.

title: The consumed case and rule-package reads have no published operation names and the MatchRequest elements are not enumerated
source: TSD P8 v2 T-A.1 and T-A.2 (API-P8-001 and API-P8-002 only, both provided); FSD P8 v3 A2.4.2 step 1 and A2.4.4; context pack P8 ownership rows (two provided operations, no consumed one); Template and Rules R4 and R7.3
description: The baseline must declare what the proceeds match reads on the other services' contracts and what the manual match carries. No source publishes the operation names: the case reference of a receipt is resolved on rwb-case and the proceeds arm of the rule package on rwb-decision, but the module appendix lists only the two provided operations of the service and the context pack confirms that no consumed operation is owned by P8. The FSD describes the step as 'receives its trigger: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer' and stops there. The request side is equally open: TSD P8 names the MatchRequest object of API-P8-002 but enumerates none of its elements. The story therefore carries both operations as placeholders with their owning service and their path base, states that the request carries the case, the account, the amount, the received date and the matched-to value and nothing else, and builds against the fakes until the owners publish the names.
evidence: TSD P8 v2 T-A.1 lists API-P8-001 GET /api/recovery/v1/proceeds and API-P8-002 POST /api/recovery/v1/proceeds/{proceedsId}/match and no consumed row; T-A.2 names 'Request: MatchRequest' with no element list; FSD P8 v3 A2.4.2 step 1 'Receives its trigger: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer'; context pack P8 'REST operations provided (2)' and no consumed section.
owner_role: P3 case owner, P7 rule owner and the P8 solution architect
proposed: Publish `GET /cases/{caseId}` (or the account-scoped case read) on rwb-case and the rule-package read with its package code on rwb-decision in the API Specification and the Service Contract Catalog, and enumerate the MatchRequest elements on API-P8-002; the story and its contract then replace the three placeholders and change no criterion.

title: No match package code, rule ID, tolerance, window, grace or priority is published for the auction, broker and LED proceeds, and payment_match_rule has no owner
source: TSD P8 v2 T3.1 (payment_match_rule, DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273) and T3.2 (LOV-MATCH-TYPE); FSD P8 v3 A2.4.3.1 (VR-P8-004-1, BR-P8-004); context pack P8 tables owned (proceeds only); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-65 and R-LIT-72
description: The match must state what it evaluates and what it records. No source gives the package code or the rule IDs of the proceeds arm, and no source publishes a value for the amount tolerance, the window before and after, the grace days or the priority. TSD P8 declares the table payment_match_rule with exactly those columns, but the ownership map gives P8 one table, proceeds, so the rows have no owner in the target. The routing logic names the outcome of a sold auction round (R-LIT-65) and the unmatched hold (R-LIT-72) without naming the mechanism. The story therefore records the rule ID and version with every answer, treats every threshold as a rule row read at run time, and holds no copy of the rule table; the package code, the rule IDs and the values stay with rwb-decision.
evidence: TSD P8 v2 T3.1 payment_match_rule DF-REF-264 amount_tolerance_pct, DF-REF-266 window_days_before, DF-REF-267 window_days_after, DF-REF-268 grace_days, DF-REF-270 priority, with no row value published; context pack P8 'Tables (1) proceeds'; TSD P8 T3.2 LOV-MATCH-TYPE EXACT, WINDOW, PARTIAL; FSD P8 v3 A2.4.3.1 BR-P8-004 'No value a business person may change is written in code'.
owner_role: P7 rule owner and the P8 solution architect
proposed: Publish the proceeds arm of the payment match package in the rule registry with its package code, its rule IDs and its values, and record in the Ownership Map whether payment_match_rule becomes a rule row of rwb-decision or a reference-data row of rwb-case; the story then cites the published package and changes no criterion.

title: The JOB-07 workflow and the matching activity have no published names, and no source fixes the trigger or the schedule form of the run
source: Context pack P8 (Jobs JOB-07 and JOB-08; Workflows 0); FSD P8 v3 A2.4.4.4 (AC-BG-P8-004-01) and A2.4.2; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-26; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-10 and DP-12
description: The slice needs one workflow and one activity, and neither has a name in any source. The context pack lists the two jobs of the service and zero workflows, the FSD says the step receives 'a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer' and its background event row gives the ACE batch of source ALS as the daily trigger, and the event design gives EV-26 as the batch-completion event read through v_ace_batch_status. Nothing states whether the run is a Temporal Schedule, an event-started workflow or a child of the case workflow, and nothing names the activity that does the match. The story declares one event-started workflow per business date on queue rwb-payment, one matching activity, and no Schedule, and it carries the two names as placeholders until their owner fixes them.
evidence: Context pack P8 'Jobs (2) JOB-07, JOB-08' and 'Workflows (0) None'; FSD P8 v3 AC-BG-P8-004-01 'ACE batch for source ALS complete (v_ace_batch_status) / Daily / Matches payments to plans'; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-26 'Consumed / ACE ingestion, read through v_ace_batch_status / payment matching (JOB-07)'.
owner_role: P8 solution architect and the workflow platform owner (RWB-PLT-WF)
proposed: Name the JOB-07 workflow and its matching activity in the Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog v1, state whether the trigger is the batch-completion event or a Schedule, and publish the input and output of the activity; the story and its contract then replace the placeholders and keep the one-transaction rule.

title: proceeds.account_payment_id points at an account_payment object that no owner of the ownership map declares
source: TSD P8 v2 T3.1 (DF-FIN-004) and T3.3 (proceeds to account_payment, many to 0 or 1); context pack P8 tables owned (proceeds only); FSD P8 v3 Data table (v_ace_payment)
description: The proceeds schema carries account_payment_id as an optional cross reference and the TSD relationship table names account_payment as its target, many to 0 or 1. No row of the ownership map declares an account_payment table, and the FSD reads the payment facts from the ACE view v_ace_payment instead. The story therefore publishes the element as a reference to the ACE payment code, resolves the payment itself on recovery.v_ace_payment, keeps no copy of an account or payment master, and declares no account_payment table; the reference and its cardinality become a gap until an owner is named.
evidence: TSD P8 v2 T3.1 DF-FIN-004 'account_payment_id | CROSS_REF | uuid | No | None | Workbench'; TSD P8 v2 T3.3 'proceeds | account_payment_id | account_payment | Many to 0 or 1'; context pack P8 tables owned: proceeds only; FSD P8 v3 A2.4 Data table lists v_ace_payment, not account_payment.
owner_role: ACE DB owner (RWB-PLT-DB) and the P8 data owner
proposed: State in the Logical Data Model and the Service Contract Catalog whether account_payment_id carries the ACE payment code of v_ace_payment and nothing else, and remove the account_payment relationship from TSD P8 T3.3 in its next version if no object is intended.
